reach_towns.label: Release 3 · Earth-tested positions and sizes · sliding 100–500 people/ha (published method)
reach_towns.note: Release 3: town POSITIONS and SIZES both tested on Earth. Positions: the earlier town rule plus a pull towards the old heartlands (800 km) beat the earlier rule in 8 of 8 regions of Han China and the Roman Empire, with the setting chosen on the other pool; 419 of 883 unmarked towns moved, every marked place stays, and the track network is rebuilt. Sizes: built-up areas follow the official catalogue of Roman cities (Hanson 2016), with Greek wall circuits counted at their inhabited share (Hansen 2008: a half, a third for large circuits). Residents = area × sliding 100–500 people/ha (published method), a density reading, not a census: 12.57 M town residents, 23.7% of the world's people, largest 246,422. Sizes follow the campaign's own ranking: capital, major cities, fortified cities, fortified towns, then unmarked towns (a lore choice). Every resident is taken from surrounding rural cells. 994 of 1034 towns (white centre) can be fed when grain may travel (34% of surplus marketed, the share that feeds 95% of Roman city residents at this density reading, Egypt included; see the grain supply map); 40 of the largest stay short. All Earth data were already used in development: cross-pool and held-out checks, not a blind test. Reach, trade and administration are rebuilt on these towns.
